neighbours.label: A word-internal piece with 'l' ('let', 'yl', 'l') inside a rare Latin or brand name that the tokenizer splits (Rhago|let|is, Nemadact|yl|us, Benadry|l)
fire: Cherry growers fear the fruit fly Rhagoletis cerasi more than any frost.
The nurse gave him a dose of Benadryl to calm the rash.
Anglers on the south coast prize the morwong Nemadactylus douglasii.
The blueberry maggot, Rhagoletis mendax, lays its eggs in ripening berries.
Foragers in the valley look for Boletus pinophilus under old pines.
A cast of Pterodactylus antiquus hangs in the museum hall.
For the bee sting she took Benadryl and held ice on her arm.
The walnut husk fly, Rhagoletis completa, arrived in Europe in the 1980s.
quiet: Cherry growers fear the fruit fly more than any frost.
The nurse gave him a dose of aspirin to calm the fever.
Anglers on the south coast prize the morwong for its firm flesh.
The blueberry maggot lays its eggs in ripening berries.
Foragers in the valley look for mushrooms under old pines.
A small booklet about flying reptiles is sold in the museum hall.
For the bee sting she took a tablet and held ice on her arm.
The violet bracelet arrived from Europe in a little box.

notes: Top pieces: 'let' x4, ' et' x3, 'l' x3, 'olid' x3. Probe: Rhagoletis 0.93, Nemadactylus 0.69, Benadryl 0.64, Boletus 0.27, Pterodactylus 0.27; Tylenol 0.03, booklet 0.01, violet 0.07. Depends on how each name is tokenized, so the new names here may not all split the same way.
